title: Asbestos respirators, protective clothing and hygiene facilities practice questions
description: Practice questions on OSHA asbestos respirator use and selection, protective clothing, laundering, decontamination and hygiene (29 CFR 1926.1101(h)-(j)).

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(h)(1), during Class II asbestos work, respirators must be used when which condition applies?

options.A: The work is performed in a building occupied by the public
options.B: The ACM is not removed in a substantially intact state
options.C: The work lasts longer than one workshift
options.D: The ACM is resilient floor covering

questions.explanation: Paragraph (h)(1)(ii) lists "Class II asbestos work when ACM is not removed in a substantially intact state."
questions.evidence: Class II asbestos work when ACM is not removed in a substantially intact state.

questions.question: Class II and III asbestos work not performed using wet methods requires respirators under (h)(1)(iii). Which work does the rule except?

options.A: Removal of TSI from pipes in a crawl space after a HEPA vacuum is used
options.B: Removal of vinyl floor tile when the room is ventilated
options.C: Class III repair of surfacing material in a single room
options.D: Removal of ACM from sloped roofs when a negative-exposure assessment has been conducted and ACM is removed in an intact state

questions.explanation: The rule excepts "removal of ACM from sloped roofs when a negative-exposure assessment has been conducted and ACM is removed in an intact state."
questions.evidence: except for removal of ACM from sloped roofs when a negative-exposure assessment has been conducted and ACM is removed in an intact state.

questions.question: A worker is doing Class IV asbestos work inside a regulated area. Under (h)(1)(vi), when must this worker use a respirator?

options.A: When employees who are performing other work in that regulated area are required to use respirators
options.B: Only when the Class IV work lasts longer than 30 minutes
options.C: Only when the worker asks for one
options.D: Only when the work is performed outdoors

questions.explanation: Respirators must be used during "Class IV asbestos work performed within regulated areas where employees who are performing other work are required to use respirators."
questions.evidence: Class IV asbestos work performed within regulated areas where employees who are performing other work are required to use respirators.

questions.question: Based on an employee's most recent medical examination, the examining physician determines that the employee will be unable to function normally while using a respirator. What does (h)(2)(ii) set?

options.A: The employee may do the work if they sign a statement accepting the risk
options.B: The employee may do the work only with a filtering facepiece respirator
options.C: The employee shall not be assigned to asbestos work that requires respirator use
options.D: The employee may do the work only under the direct supervision of the competent person

questions.explanation: "No employee shall be assigned to asbestos work that requires respirator use if, based on their most recent medical examination, the examining physician determines that the employee will be unable to function normally while using a respirator."
questions.evidence: No employee shall be assigned to asbestos work that requires respirator use if, based on their most recent medical examination, the examining physician determines that the employee will be unable to function normally while using a respirator

questions.question: An employee who cannot use a respirator is offered an available transfer position under (h)(2)(ii). What must that position be?

options.A: With the same employer, in the same geographical area, and with the same seniority, status, rate of pay, and other job benefits
options.B: With any employer in the same State, at the same rate of pay
options.C: With the same employer at any location, with seniority starting over
options.D: With the same employer, at a rate of pay set by the examining physician

questions.explanation: The rule says the transfer position "must be with the same employer, in the same geographical area, and with the same seniority, status, rate of pay, and other job benefits the employee had just prior to such transfer."
questions.evidence: it must be with the same employer, in the same geographical area, and with the same seniority, status, rate of pay, and other job benefits the employee had just prior to such transfer.

questions.question: Which type of respirator does (h)(3)(i)(A) say employers must not select or use against asbestos fibers?

options.A: Tight-fitting powered air-purifying respirators
options.B: Full facepiece supplied-air respirators
options.C: Air-purifying half mask respirators with HEPA filters
options.D: Filtering facepiece respirators

questions.explanation: Employers "must not select or use filtering facepiece respirators for use against asbestos fibers."
questions.evidence: employers must not select or use filtering facepiece respirators for use against asbestos fibers.

questions.question: An employee who would be given a negative pressure respirator chooses to use a tight-fitting PAPR, and the PAPR provides adequate protection. What does (h)(3)(ii) require of the employer?

options.A: To refuse, because the respirator was already selected
options.B: To provide the PAPR instead of the negative pressure respirator
options.C: To allow the PAPR only if the employee buys it
options.D: To provide a supplied-air respirator instead

questions.explanation: Employers "must provide an employee with tight-fitting, powered air-purifying respirator (PAPR) instead of a negative pressure respirator ... when the employee chooses to use a PAPR and it provides adequate protection to the employee."
questions.evidence: Employers must provide an employee with tight-fitting, powered air-purifying respirator (PAPR) instead of a negative pressure respirator

questions.question: A crew performs Class III asbestos work that disturbs TSI. Which respirator does (h)(3)(iii) require the employer to provide?

options.A: A filtering facepiece respirator
options.B: A full facepiece supplied-air respirator with an auxiliary positive-pressure SCBA
options.C: An air-purifying half mask respirator, other than a filtering facepiece respirator
options.D: No respirator, as long as wet methods are used

questions.explanation: Employers must provide "an air-purifying half mask respirator, other than a filtering facepiece respirator," whenever employees perform "Class III asbestos work involving disturbance of TSI or surfacing ACM or PACM."
questions.evidence: Class III asbestos work involving disturbance of TSI or surfacing ACM or PACM.

questions.question: Employees in a regulated area perform Class I asbestos work with no negative exposure assessment available, and the exposure assessment indicates exposure above 1 f/cc as an 8-hour TWA. What does (h)(3)(iv)(B) require the employer to provide?

options.A: A full facepiece supplied-air respirator operated in the pressure-demand mode and equipped with an auxiliary positive-pressure SCBA
options.B: A tight-fitting powered air-purifying respirator with HEPA filters
options.C: An air-purifying half mask respirator with HEPA filters
options.D: A filtering facepiece respirator worn under a face shield

questions.explanation: For exposure "above 1 f/cc as an 8-hour TWA," the employer must provide "A full facepiece supplied-air respirator operated in the pressure-demand mode and equipped with an auxiliary positive-pressure SCBA."
questions.evidence: A full facepiece supplied-air respirator operated in the pressure-demand mode and equipped with an auxiliary positive-pressure SCBA

questions.question: Under (i)(1), protective clothing is required for any employee performing Class I operations that involve removal of how much TSI or surfacing ACM and PACM?

options.A: Over 1 linear or 1 square foot
options.B: Over 100 linear or 50 square feet
options.C: Over 3 linear or 3 square feet
options.D: Over 25 linear or 10 square feet

questions.explanation: Protective clothing is required "for any employee performing Class I operations which involve the removal of over 25 linear or 10 square feet of TSI or surfacing ACM and PACM."
questions.evidence: for any employee performing Class I operations which involve the removal of over 25 linear or 10 square feet of TSI or surfacing ACM and PACM.

questions.question: An employer gives contaminated clothing to an outside laundry. What does (i)(2)(ii) require the employer to do?

options.A: Obtain a written laundering certificate from the competent person
options.B: Inform the laundry of the requirement to effectively prevent the release of airborne asbestos in excess of the TWA and excursion limit
options.C: Have the clothing washed twice before it leaves the site
options.D: Send the clothing only in open bins so the laundry can inspect it

questions.explanation: The employer "shall inform such person of the requirement in paragraph (i)(2)(i) of this section to effectively prevent the release of airborne asbestos in excess of the TWA and excursion limit."
questions.evidence: Any employer who gives contaminated clothing to another person for laundering shall inform such person of the requirement in paragraph (i)(2)(i) of this section to effectively prevent the release of airborne asbestos in excess of the TWA and excursion limit

questions.question: How does (i)(3) say contaminated clothing must be transported?

options.A: In cloth laundry bags tied at the top
options.B: In an open hamper lined with plastic
options.C: In sealed impermeable bags, or other closed, impermeable containers, labeled in accordance with paragraph (k)
options.D: Folded inside out in the cab of a work vehicle

questions.explanation: "Contaminated clothing shall be transported in sealed impermeable bags, or other closed, impermeable containers, and be labeled in accordance with paragraph (k) of this section."
questions.evidence: Contaminated clothing shall be transported in sealed impermeable bags, or other closed, impermeable containers, and be labeled in accordance with paragraph (k) of this section.

questions.question: Under (i)(4)(i), who must examine the worksuits worn by employees for rips or tears?

options.A: The competent person
options.B: The examining physician
options.C: Each employee's coworker on the same crew
options.D: The laundry that cleans the worksuits

questions.explanation: "The competent person shall examine worksuits worn by employees at least once per workshift for rips or tears that may occur during performance of work."
questions.evidence: The competent person shall examine worksuits worn by employees at least once per workshift for rips or tears

questions.topic: Decontamination areas for larger Class I jobs
questions.question: On a Class I job removing over 25 linear feet of TSI, what does (j)(1)(i) say the decontamination area consists of?

options.A: A clean room and a lunch area
options.B: An area covered by an impermeable drop cloth
options.C: A shower trailer parked anywhere on the site
options.D: An equipment room, shower area, and clean room in series

questions.explanation: "The decontamination area shall consist of an equipment room, shower area, and clean room in series."
questions.evidence: The decontamination area shall consist of an equipment room, shower area, and clean room in series.

questions.topic: Decontamination areas for larger Class I jobs
questions.question: On a large Class I job, the employer demonstrates that the shower cannot feasibly be located between the equipment room and the clean room. Which is one of the options (j)(1)(i)(B) gives for what employees must do?

options.A: Skip the shower if they change into street clothes outdoors
options.B: Remove asbestos contamination from their worksuits in the equipment room using a HEPA vacuum before proceeding to a shower that is not adjacent to the work area
options.C: Blow off their worksuits with compressed air and shower at home
options.D: Wear their worksuits to the nearest public restroom to wash

questions.explanation: Employees must "Remove asbestos contamination from their worksuits in the equipment room using a HEPA vacuum before proceeding to a shower that is not adjacent to the work area; or" remove their contaminated worksuits and don clean ones first.
questions.evidence: Remove asbestos contamination from their worksuits in the equipment room using a HEPA vacuum before proceeding to a shower that is not adjacent to the work area; or

questions.topic: Decontamination entry, exit and lunch areas
questions.question: Under the decontamination area entry procedures in (j)(1)(ii), what must employees do before leaving the clean room?

options.A: Shower
options.B: HEPA vacuum their street clothing
options.C: Put on protective clothing and respiratory protection
options.D: Remove gross contamination from their equipment

questions.explanation: The employer shall ensure that employees "Put on protective clothing and respiratory protection before leaving the clean room."
questions.evidence: Put on protective clothing and respiratory protection before leaving the clean room.

questions.topic: Decontamination entry, exit and lunch areas
questions.question: Under the exit procedures in (j)(1)(iii), in which room does the rule say employees shall not remove their respirators?

options.A: The clean room
options.B: The lunch area
options.C: The shower area
options.D: The equipment room

questions.explanation: "Employees shall not remove their respirators in the equipment room."
questions.evidence: Employees shall not remove their respirators in the equipment room.

questions.topic: Decontamination entry, exit and lunch areas
questions.question: Food and beverages are consumed at a worksite where employees are performing Class I asbestos work. What does (j)(1)(iv) require of the lunch areas the employer provides?

options.A: Airborne concentrations of asbestos below the permissible exposure limit and/or excursion limit
options.B: A location inside the regulated area next to the clean room
options.C: A HEPA-filtered air supply checked by the competent person
options.D: Lockers for each employee's street clothing

questions.explanation: The employer "shall provide lunch areas in which the airborne concentrations of asbestos are below the permissible exposure limit and/or excursion limit."
questions.evidence: the employer shall provide lunch areas in which the airborne concentrations of asbestos are below the permissible exposure limit and/or excursion limit.

questions.topic: Hygiene for smaller jobs, Class II, III and IV work, and smoking
questions.question: Class II asbestos work is done with no negative exposure assessment produced before the operation. Under (j)(2)(i), what does the equipment room or area consist of?

options.A: An equipment room, shower area, and clean room in series
options.B: An area covered by an impermeable drop cloth on the floor or horizontal working surface
options.C: A lunch area with filtered air
options.D: A locker room at least 50 feet from the regulated area

questions.explanation: The equipment room or area "shall consist of an area covered by an impermeable drop cloth on the floor or horizontal working surface."
questions.evidence: which shall consist of an area covered by an impermeable drop cloth on the floor or horizontal working surface.

questions.topic: Hygiene for smaller jobs, Class II, III and IV work, and smoking
questions.question: Employees perform Class IV work within a regulated area where Class I work is also under way. What hygiene practice does (j)(3) require them to follow?

options.A: Only the no-smoking rule in (j)(4)
options.B: Their own hygiene plan, chosen by each employee
options.C: The hygiene practice required of employees performing work which has a higher classification within that regulated area
options.D: No hygiene practice, because Class IV is maintenance and custodial work

questions.explanation: Employers "shall ensure that employees performing Class IV work within a regulated area comply with the hygiene practice required of employees performing work which has a higher classification within that regulated area."
questions.evidence: comply with the hygiene practice required of employees performing work which has a higher classification within that regulated area.
